headline_marked: [[GLM-5.3 hits API]] at $1.40/$4.40 per million tokens, offering competitive frontier AI
headline: GLM-5.3 hits API at $1.40/$4.40 per million tokens, offering competitive frontier AI
summary: Z.ai's GLM-5.3, known for its advanced cyber capabilities, is now available via API at $1.40 input and $4.40 output per million tokens, positioning it below premium frontier models.
details: Chinese startup z.ai has launched its GLM-5.3 language model on its API, priced at $1.40 per million input tokens and $4.40 per million output tokens. This allows developers to integrate the model into their applications, building on its advanced cyber capabilities.

The pricing remains consistent with the previous GLM-5.2 version, despite claims of substantially stronger coding and long-horizon agent performance. This positions GLM-5.3 significantly below several high-end frontier APIs like GPT-5.6 Sol ($35) and Claude Opus 5 ($30) for a comparable workload.

While not the absolute cheapest, it offers a strong balance. For instance, Google's Gemini 3.7 Flash is $0.75 input and $3.75 output, and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Luna is $0.20 input and $1.20 output, though these are often introductory or lower-tier models.

Artificial Analysis gives GLM-5.3 an Intelligence Index score of 60, tying Kimi K3 as the top-performing open weights model. However, the analysis also notes GLM-5.3 is more verbose than its predecessor, meaning identical per-token rates don't always translate to flat costs for a completed task.

For developers, this means a new, powerful, and relatively low-cost option for testing frontier-class coding and agent workloads is immediately available. Z.ai plans to make the model's weights openly available, but a precise date is pending.

headline_marked: [[GTA 6 gameplay leaked]] ahead of its new trailer, and Rockstar is taking down the videos
headline: GTA 6 gameplay leaked ahead of its new trailer, and Rockstar is taking down the videos
summary: Two minute-long gameplay clips and a map of Leonida from Grand Theft Auto VI have reportedly surfaced online, prompting Rockstar Games to issue DMCA takedowns.
details: Two minute-long gameplay clips and a detailed map of Leonida, GTA VI's Florida-inspired setting, have reportedly leaked online. Rockstar Games is actively issuing DMCA takedown notices to those sharing the footage.

The leaked map, named Leonida, appears as a compact version of south Florida, featuring a large city (Rockstar's Miami) on the east and extensive greenspace. Numerous islands, resembling the Florida Keys, are dotted across the south, with markers indicating homes, vehicles, and even alligators.

One clip shows Jason, a protagonist, at a waterside home, engaging in activities like basketball which grants a 'focus stat boost'. This suggests the inclusion of RPG mechanics, reminiscent of GTA San Andreas workouts.

The clip's HUD shows dollar values in the top right and a focus bar when Jason holds the basketball. The building in the footage matches an official screenshot, identified as Jason's safehouse on the game's website.

The second clip features Jason causing mild carnage after a U-turn, leading to a fight with a delivery truck driver. Jason kills the driver with a wrench, earning a two-star wanted level and depleting an energy bar with each swing.

A devil icon with a minus sign appears, hinting at an honor/karma system similar to Red Dead Redemption. Prompts for 'loadout' and 'storage' suggest weapon changes and item storage in cars, while a gas meter indicates vehicles will require fueling.

While the clips are plausible, their legitimacy and age remain unconfirmed, especially given Rockstar's server breach earlier this year. The alleged leaker claims the release is a protest against anti-consumer practices like digital-only physical editions and threatens further action.
Grand Theft Auto VI is officially set to launch on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S on November 19. An extended look at the game will first stream on Netflix on August 27.
